full_text:
The 2026 NFL season is just around the corner, which means more NFL player props are being released with each passing week. I previously broke down the [2026 NFL Passing Yards Props](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/2026/nfl-player-props-passing-yards#/), and it’s time to dive into the 2026 NFL Passing Yards Leader odds for the top quarterbacks. In this article, I highlighted a bet I’ve already dropped in our Betting Discord and a couple of additional wagers I considered.

__Matthew Stafford__ cashed the 10th-shortest odds at +2000 by throwing for an NFL-best 4707 yards last season. He beat out __Jared Goff__ (4564, +800) and __Dak Prescott__ (4552, +800) for the honor, who were the only other QBs to throw for 4500+ yards. __Joe Burrow__, Goff, and Prescott are the co-favorites to finish as the league leader in passing yards at +800 odds. The defending champion Stafford (+1000) is the only other quarterback with his longest odds at 14/1 or shorter.

\>Be sure to check out [Brolley’s Best Bets: 2026 NFL Futures](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/series/2025/best-bets) for my favorite futures bets all offseason…Subscribe to the Best Bets Podcast on your [favorite platform](https://www.fantasypoints.com/media/podcasts/show/nfl-best-bets) and on [YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/@FantasyPointsBetting) for year-round NFL betting talk…Join our “#official-bets” [Fantasy Points Discord](https://www.fantasypoints.com/media/discord) to see our staff's wagers as soon as we make them!

Passing Yards Leaders from the Last Decade
------------------------------------------

#### __Historical Hints__

The favorite hasn’t led the league in passing yards since __Drew Brees__ did it back in 2016 at +525 odds. The eventual leader has come from inside the top five in odds in seven of the last 10 years, including __Joe Burrow__ at +850 (5th) two seasons ago. __Matthew Stafford__ came from further down the board at +2000 odds (10th) last season. He joined __Tua Tagovailoa__ (2023) and __Deshaun Watson__ (2020) at the longest odds to lead the league in the last decade.

The league leader has skewed younger in recent years, with five of the last seven winners checking in at 28 years old or younger. Stafford (2025) and __Tom Brady__ (2021) were the exceptions at 38 and 44 years old, respectively. The league leader in passing yards has reached 4700+ yards in eight of the last 10 years, with only Tua (4624) and Brady (4577) failing to reach that mark. This year’s leader will likely have to average at least 275+ yards per game in 16-17 games to get the job done.

2026 NFL Passing Yards Leader Odds
----------------------------------

\>The table is sorted by [Fantasy Points passing yards projection](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/projections/season/qb). You should target the Longest Odds for Most Rushing TDs to maximize your potential return. I used odds from DraftKings (DK), BetMGM (MGM), Caesars (CZR), theSCORE Bet (Score), and Bet365 (365) as of July 14.

Brolley’s Leans
---------------

#### __{{Jared Goff|QB|LAC|17922}}__ (LAC) most regular season passing yards (+800, BetMGM)

+ __Why I like Goff__: Will 2026 finally be the year that Goff leads the league in passing yards? He finished as the runner-up in the market in three straight seasons, and reached 4400+ passing yards in four straight seasons since the Lions became a winning team. Goff is averaging 34.0 attempts/game (8th), 7.88 YPA (5th), and 267.7 passing YPG (2nd) since 2022. Goff and the Lions will face the NFL’s easiest schedule based on NFL season win totals, and the Lions have the third-highest [implied team total](https://x.com/ConnorAllenNFL/status/2057527213222727779?s=20) based on Vegas lines for the upcoming season. Goff should play in plenty of shootouts because of a defense that’s taken some steps back in recent seasons.

+ __Why I ultimately passed__: Goff’s odds aren’t long enough to bet on him to finally break through in this market. He’ll be working with a new playcaller for the third straight season after Dan Campbell took over playcalling halfway through last season from John Morton. The Lions brought in Drew Petzing, who called the most pass-heavy offense (7.3% PROE) with the Cardinals last season, but he threw it so much out of pure desperation. Michael Carter led Arizona’s pitiful rushing attack with 333 yards, and Arizona’s defense couldn’t slow any team down. Petzing ranked ahead of only Arthur Smith and Shane Steichen in PROE (-2.2%) from 2023-24.

#### __{{Justin Herbert|QB|LAC|21681}}__ (LAC) most regular season passing yards (+3000, Bet365)

+ __Why I like Herbert__: He’s yet to win the passing yards crown in his first six seasons, but he’s come close to doing it twice. He owns a pair of runner-up finishes in 2021-22 when he totaled 9753 yards over two seasons. Herbert has the 11th-best odds to lead the league in passing yards, but he checks in with the fifth-most passing yards in our projections. The Chargers hired Mike McDaniel to call the offense, who previously helped Tua Tagovailoa lead the NFL with 4624 passing yards in 2023 during his time in Miami. Herbert will be a more efficient passer under McDaniel after Miami ranked 6th in YPA (7.58) during McDaniel’s four-year run as head coach, mostly with Tua at quarterback.
+ __Why I ultimately passed__: Herbert ranks fifth in passing yards in our projections, but he’s a clear tier below the four favorites and is leading a tightly packed group of six QBs in the second tier. We have high expectations for this Chargers offense overall based on our projections. I previously bet on Omarion Hampton [at +2800 odds](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/betting/2026/nfl-player-props-rushing-yards-leader#/) to lead the NFL in rushing yards, and McDaniel wants to keep defenses on their toes with a balanced attack. Los Angeles is ready to run the rock more effectively, swapping out Keenan Allen for heavier personnel options in Alec Ingold, Charlie Kolar, and David Njoku. Herbert has been trending in the wrong direction over the past three seasons, averaging 32.0 attempts/game and 233.3 passing YPG in 2023-25 compared to 40.1 attempts/game and 287.5 passing YPG in 2020-22.

#### __{{Tyler Shough|QB|NO|23187}}__ (NO) most regular season passing yards (+2200, Bet365)

+ __Why I like Shough__: Shough reached 17.1+ FP and 239+ passing yards in seven of his final eight starts despite a weak receiving corps behind Chris Olave, ranking as the QB9 (18.8) from Week 10 on. New Orleans needed to determine if Shough is the quarterback of the future, and they selected Jordyn Tyson eighth overall to get a proper evaluation. Tyson was one of the late risers in the draft process despite concerns about durability and effort. Brett Whitefield saw shades of CeeDee Lamb in Tyson’s play style, and he’ll immediately slot in next to Olave. Shough could take a major step forward in Kellen Moore’s fantasy-friendly offense, which played at the NFL’s fastest pace last season. They averaged a play every 26.6 seconds, which led to the 11th-most plays/game (63.2).
+ __Why I ultimately passed__: I wanted to bet Shough to win the passing yards crown, but his odds came in much shorter than I expected. He showed real potential as a 26-year-old rookie, but he doesn’t have a full season of starts under his belt after starting the final nine games. Tyson and Olave will form a high-upside young tandem, but they also have some major durability concerns. Tyson suffered a multi-ligament knee injury early in his college career, and he’s dealt with ongoing hamstring issues since last season, which limited him in the pre-draft process. Olave suffered multiple concussions during the 2024 season and just went off blood thinners in late June for a blood clot that was discovered in his lung before the 2025 season finale.

#### __{{Kyler Murray|QB|MIN|20889}}__ (Min) most regular season passing yards (+15000, Bet365)

+ __Why I like Murray__: This bet is worth a small sprinkle if you have a Bet365 account at these outlier odds. Other sportsbooks have Murray lined between +4000-5000 odds to win this market. Kevin O’Connell’s offenses ranked in the top six in passing yards and pass rate over expectation in each of his first three seasons as head coach before last year’s quarterback situation undermined the entire offense. He could get back to his pass-happy ways with a competent triggerman, and his system propelled Sam Darnold to a career revival in 2024. He averaged 7.9 YPA and 254.1 passing YPG to finish fifth in the race for the most passing yards with 4319. Justin Jefferson can single-handedly propel Murray to the top of the passing yards leaderboard. He reached 1400+ yards in his first four full seasons before last year’s disappointing campaign.
+ __Why I ultimately passed__: Kyler is expected to easily win this open competition against J.J. McCarthy, but that doesn’t mean his career isn’t trending in the wrong direction. He’s never reached 4000+ passing yards in his first seven seasons, and he’s topped 7.1 YPA for a season just once in his career. He’s coming off career lows in YPA (6.0), QBR (47.2), and sack rate (9.04%) before essentially being benched after five weeks. He finished fifth in completion percentage (68.3%) but 39th in YPA (5.98) and 42nd in aDOT (6.3) among 45 QBs who attempted 100+ passes. The best ability is availability, and Murray has played 12 or more games just once over his last four seasons.

Brolley’s Best Bets
-------------------

{{PAYWALL}}

#### __{{Drake Maye|QB|NE|24958}}__ (NE) most regular season passing yards (+1500, DraftKings/BetMGM)

\>Risk .3 units to win 4.5 units. [Placed July 15](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/2026/brolleys-best-bets-nfl-futures).

Maye finished one first-place vote short of beating out __Matthew Stafford__ for the MVP award in just his second season after leading the Patriots to 14 victories. He ranked fourth with 4394 passing yards despite ranking 12th with 492 attempts (28.9 A/G). He averaged 99.7 fewer attempts than the three QBs who finished ahead of him (Stafford, __Jared Goff__, and __Dak Prescott__), even with the Patriots ranking fifth in pass rate over expectation (5.4%).

Maye took full advantage of the NFL’s easiest schedules as half of New England’s victories came by double-digit margins, but it limited his passing production late in games — 18.8% of his yards came in the fourth quarter. New England will face a tougher schedule — it’s still the [12th-easiest based on win totals](https://www.sharpfootballanalysis.com/analysis/nfl-strength-of-schedule/) — and it should lead to more competitive gamescripts and more opportunities for an upgraded passing attack. Maye led the NFL in YPA (8.93) and completion percentage (72%), and ranked third in catchable throw rate (79.3%) with a 32-year-old __Stefon Diggs__ leading a hodge-podge receiving corps.

__Eliot Wolf__ aggressively upgraded New England’s WRs, signing __Romeo Doubs__ at the start of free agency, who immediately jumped ahead of __Kayshon Boutte__ and __Mack Hollins__ on the perimeter. He then traded for __A.J. Brown__ on June 1, who gives Maye a true #1 WR. He finished ninth in target share (27.5%) and eighth in first-read share (35%) last season, and is averaging 76.5 receiving YPG in his seven-year career. Maye already ranked first in YPA (9.98) and EPA/DB (.51) against man coverage in 2025, and he’ll get the NFL’s best man-beater in YPRR (3.69) and TPRR (.36) during his time in Philadelphia from 2022-25. Maye is priced slightly down the board from the favorites, but a motivated and healthy Brown could elevate him into contention for the passing yards crown.
